bib.title: Beyond Ten Turns: Unlocking Long-Horizon Agentic Search with Large-Scale Asynchronous RL

question: How can online RL unlock expert-level 'Search Intelligence' in open-source search agents given small turn limits and scarce hard QA data?
hypothesis: Small turn limits (<=10) and poor data prevent online RL from learning complex search strategies; relaxing the limit with asynchronous RL and synthetic hard QA will unlock them.
contributions: Fully asynchronous agentic RL training enabling long-horizon search (128 turns) with high efficiency
A prompt-based LLM data-synthesis agent producing challenging, grounded QA pairs
ASearcher-Local-7B/14B and ASearcher-Web-QwQ open-source agents with state-of-the-art open-source results

method.summary: ASearcher trains search agents (search + browse tools) with GRPO in a fully asynchronous RL system built on AReaL, allowing up to 128 turns per trajectory for QwQ-32B, with a sparse trajectory-end reward (format x F1 for base models, LLM-as-Judge for QwQ). Training data are filtered HotpotQA/2Wiki plus a data-synthesis agent that injects facts and fuzzes details; Qwen2.5-7B/14B are trained on a local Wikipedia RAG and QwQ-32B on the live web.
method.task: agentic search / multi-hop and single-hop QA, deep-research benchmarks

datasets.name: HotpotQA + 2WikiMultiHopQA (filtered)
datasets.preprocessing: RL-trained model answers 16 times per question; drop if 0 correct of 16, if accuracy >=50%, or if solved with <=1 search turn

datasets.name: ASearcher synthetic QA
datasets.size: 25,624 entries from 14,107 seed questions (intro: 134k generated, 25.6k need tools)
datasets.source: LLM synthesis agent; Wikipedia facts injected; verified by LLM and QwQ-32B
datasets.preprocessing: Quality check, difficulty via QwQ-32B no-tool answers, answer-uniqueness check; drop questions QwQ answers without tools

datasets.name: Final training sets
datasets.size: two sets of 35k each (one for 7B/14B, one for QwQ-32B)
datasets.preprocessing: stage 2 for QwQ keeps only questions needing >=5 tool calls

datasets.name: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue, Bamboogle
datasets.size: 1000 random instances from validation sets of HotpotQA, 2Wiki, MuSiQue; full test sets for Bamboogle

datasets.name: GAIA, xBench-DeepSearch, Frames, HLE-500
datasets.size: GAIA: 103 text-only validation examples; others full test sets

models.name: ASearcher-Web-QwQ
models.context: input kept to at most 10k tokens (last 25k characters of history); thinking discarded from history

other.use: external webpage summariser and K=16 answer aggregator at test time only

models.name: Search-R1 7B/14B/32B, R1-Searcher-7B, Search-o1(QwQ), DeepResearcher, SimpleDeepSearcher, WebThinker-QwQ, WebDancer-32B

training.objective: GRPO with token-level normalised clipped objective (Eq. 1); dynamic filtering removes queries whose responses all get identical reward; sparse trajectory-end reward: format x F1 for base LLMs, LLM-as-Judge (no format reward) for QwQ; all generated tokens (thinking, tool calls, summaries) trained end to end

other.system: fully asynchronous rollouts and decoupled rollout/training, built on AReaL; training step launches as soon as enough trajectories form a batch
other.curriculum: two-stage for QwQ: stage 1 all difficulties; stage 2 only questions needing >=5 tool calls
other.group_size_G: not stated (16 responses used for data filtering only)
other.off_policy_staleness: not stated; trajectories can span multiple model versions
other.training_steps_hint: Fig 6 shows around 200 steps where stage 2 starts (read from text 'after step 200')

inference.samples: Avg@4 and Pass@4 over 4 runs on GAIA/xBench/Frames; baselines run with official code for 4 seeds; test-time search K=16 runs aggregated by DeepSeek-V3
inference.prompting: Base LLMs: append-only history from system prompt, tags such as <search>query</search>; QwQ: separate prompts for tool selection, summarisation, answering; history keeps summarised thoughts and tool calls only, last 25k characters
inference.retrieval: Local: Wikipedia 2018 corpus (DPR) via RAG; web: search engine returning snippets+URLs, browser returning page content summarised by the agent; retriever/search backend, top-k not stated

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: word-level harmonic mean of precision and recall vs reference answer

metrics.name: LLM-as-Judge (LasJ)
metrics.definition: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judges correctness per task-specific instructions

metrics.name: Pass@4
metrics.definition: ratio of questions where the agent finds the correct answer in 4 trials

eval.protocol: Fair comparison: baselines use same tools; 4 runs for the hard benchmarks; no significance tests or confidence intervals reported; single training run (no seeds stated)

evidence.quote: The batch size is set as 128 for 7B and 14B models, and 64 for ASearcher-Web-QwQ.

results.claim: ASearcher-Web-QwQ-v2 reaches Avg@4 58.7 on GAIA (103 text-only val examples).
results.setup: ASearcher-Web-QwQ (QwQ-32B, web search+browse tools, turn limit 128), LLM-as-Judge, Avg@4 over 4 runs, GAIA text-only validation subset
results.note: Table 4 row ASearcher-Web-QwQ-v2, column GAIA Avg@4
results.quote: achieves the best Avg@4 scores on GAIA (58.7)

results.setup: ASearcher-Web-QwQ (QwQ-32B, web search+browse tools, turn limit 128), LLM-as-Judge, Avg@4 over 4 runs

results.claim: RL training lifts the QwQ-32B agent by +15.0 GAIA, +22.4 xBench, and Frames (text says +14.6, Fig 1 caption says +15.6).
results.setup: QwQ-32B agent before vs after RL, Avg@4, Fig 8
results.note: Fig 1 caption prints +15.6 for Frames; Sec 4.2 prints +14.6. Intro also says '78.0% and 34.3% improvements' on xBench and GAIA (relative, apparently).
results.where: Sec 4.2 Effect of RL Training; Fig 1; Fig 8
results.quote: obtains +15.0, +22.4, and +14.6 improvements on GAIA, xBench-DeepSearch and Frames respectively

results.claim: Pass@4 for ASearcher-Web-QwQ-v2 is 74.7 on GAIA and 75.0 on xBench-DeepSearch.
results.setup: ASearcher-Web-QwQ (QwQ-32B, web search+browse tools, turn limit 128), LLM-as-Judge, Pass@4 (fraction of questions solved in any of 4 trials)
results.quote: ASearcher-Web-QwQ achieves 74.7 on GAIA and 75.0 on xBench-DeepSearch

results.claim: Accuracy improves when the agent is forced to use more minimum turns (test-time sweep), supporting that complex tasks need long trajectories; no numbers given in text, read only from Fig 6 Left.
results.setup: RL-trained QwQ-32B agent, minimum-turn enforcement, accuracy averaged over GAIA, xBench-DeepSearch, Frames
results.note: This is a forced-minimum-turns sweep at test time, not a training-time turn-cap ablation. The paper has no matched short-cap training ablation.
results.quote: The results demonstrate that accuracy improves with more turns, confirming that complex tasks demand longer trajectories for effective problem-solving.

results.claim: Training reached tool calls exceeding 100 turns and output tokens exceeding 400k (abstract/Fig 1), but Sec 4.3 says QwQ agent averaged max about 40 calls at step 200, peaks of 70 calls, and over 150k tokens.
results.note: Sec 4.3: 'reaching a maximum of around 40 calls at the 200th step, with peak instances even achieving up to 70 calls' and 'a maximum of over 150k tokens'. The two statements are not reconciled in the text; the 100/400k figure probably refers to individual longest trajectories (Fig 1 middle/right), unconfirmed.
results.quote: tool calls exceeding 100 turns and output tokens exceeding 400k during training time

results.claim: Local-trained ASearcher-Local-7B beats Search-R1-7B and R1-Searcher-7B on the local-KB suite (avg F1 58.0 vs 54.3 and 52.2; LasJ 61.0 vs 55.4 and 54.7).
results.setup: Qwen2.5-7B base, RL on local Wikipedia-2018 RAG, 7 QA benchmarks, 1000 sampled instances for HotpotQA/2Wiki/MuSiQue
results.quote: an average F1 of 58.0, outperforming strong baselines such as Search-R1-7B

results.claim: ASearcher-Local-14B local-KB average: text says F1 60.0 and LasJ 65.6, Table 2 prints 59.7 and 63.6.
results.note: Table 2 row ASearcher-Local-14B Avg: 59.7 and 63.6; the text's 60.0 and 65.6 match the Table 3 (web setting) row for the same model. The text appears to quote the wrong table.
results.quote: ASearcher-Local-14B reaches an F1 of 60.0 and LasJ of 65.6

results.claim: Local-trained agents transfer zero-shot to the web setting: ASearcher-Web-14B avg F1 61.5.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-14B, trained on web, evaluated in web search+browse setting
results.quote: ASearcher-Web-14B achieves the best performance with an average F1
results.table: Table 3, row ASearcher-Web-14B, column Avg. F1

results.claim: Using DeepSeek-V3 as webpage summariser (zero-shot swap) raises GAIA 58.7 to 60.3 and xBench 51.1 to 56.4; test-time search K=16 with DeepSeek-V3 aggregation reaches 71.8 GAIA, 75.0 xBench, 83.4 Frames, 24.6 HLE-500.
results.setup: Pass@1 table; ASearcher-Web-QwQ-v2, K=16 independent runs aggregated by DeepSeek-V3
results.note: Baselines in Table 5 (o3, Claude-4-Sonnet, Kimi-Researcher...) are from official reports (dagger), not rerun; Table 5 text extraction is column-misaligned so only ASearcher rows were taken.
results.quote: we run K = 16 independent runs for each problem in the test set and aggregate the conclusions from these independent runs with DeepSeek-V3
results.table: Table 5, row + Test-time Search (K=16), columns GAIA, xBench-DeepSearch

results.claim: Two-stage curriculum: stage 2 keeps only questions needing at least 5 tool calls; v1 to v2 gives GAIA 52.8 to 58.7, xBench 42.1 to 51.1.
results.note: v1 to v2 also adds more training steps, so the gain is not isolated to the data filter.
results.quote: we retain only the questions that require at least 5 tool calls to solve

results.claim: 7B model fails to learn webpage browsing while 14B does; query count scales to about 6.
results.note: Authors' hypothesis for 7B browsing failure (capacity) is untested.
results.quote: the number of search queries scale up to 6

results.claim: Training ASearcher-Web-QwQ takes about 16k H800 GPU hours.
results.quote: Training of ASearcher-Web-QwQ takes approximated 16k H800 GPU hours in total

results.claim: Data synthesis: 14,107 seeds yield 25,624 selected questions (avg 4.27 injections, 2.10 fuzzes).
results.setup: Synthesis agent, up to three variations kept per seed
results.note: Intro says 'From 14k seed QAs, we generate 134k high-quality samples, with 25.6k requiring external tools'; 134k is not defined in Sec 3.2.2.
results.quote: Starting with 14,107 seed questions, we perform an average of 6.3 injections and 3.2 fuzzes per question

results.claim: Open-source data filtered from 304k QA pairs to 16k challenging samples for RL.
results.setup: HotpotQA + 2WikiMultiHopQA, filtered with an RL-trained model, 16 responses per question
results.quote: from a total of 304k QA pairs, we retain 16k challenging samples for RL training

limits: No matched ablation of the training-time turn cap (e.g. 10 vs 128) or of asynchronous vs batch training on final accuracy; efficiency claim for async is shown only schematically in Fig 7.
Value for the 'long horizon matters' claim is a test-time forced-minimum-turn sweep plus a case study (Fig 3/12) on a single GAIA question.
Optimizer, learning rate, group size G, clip epsilon, steps, decoding settings, seeds are not stated; one training run, no variance across training seeds.
Text and tables disagree in places (Frames gain +14.6 vs +15.6; ASearcher-Local-14B 60.0/65.6 in text vs 59.7/63.6 in Table 2; 100+ turns/400k tokens vs max ~40 calls/150k tokens in Sec 4.3).
Table 5 commercial baselines come from official reports and may use different protocols; DeepSeek-V3 summariser and K=16 aggregation use an external LLM.
Authors' explanation for the 7B model failing to learn browsing (small capacity) is a hypothesis only.
